characters.name: Beth Ann Stanton
characters.description: A meek and dutiful suburban housewife whose cheery demeanor hides a lot of pain. She then is shocked to discover her husband is cheating on her with a diner waitress and decides to befriend the waitress under a different name. '50s Hair: Beth Ann starts out with a curly bob in the style of the decade while Rob wears his hair slicked. This is to showcase the beginning of Beth Ann's transformation from a mousy woman to someone in charge of her destiny. Becoming the Mask: Beth Ann initially befriends April, so that she can get closer to her and drive her away from Rob. But she soon starts to genuinely enjoy spending time with her and soon becomes invested in helping her. Beware the Nice Ones: There's hints early on that cheerful, prudish Beth Ann has more going on beneath the surface, but as the series goes on it becomes clear how close she is to snapping and becoming violent.Namely, she's the only one of the three who actually commits murder: Simone performs aMercy Killat her husband's request and Taylor kills Jade in self-defense, but Beth Ann actually sets Rob up to die and smiles as he does. Chekhov's Gun: She buys a gun and shows it to Rob, claiming it's for self-defense after an alleged robbery that occurred to one of their neighbors. She then shows him that she will keep it in the kitchen drawer for emergencies and demonstrates that she loaded it already. During his scuffle with Ralph, Beth Ann rushes over to get the gun and tosses it over to Rob.But when he tries to shoot the gun, it's revealed that Beth Anntook out the bullets ahead of time. Which leads to Ralph firing off his own gun and killing Rob.

characters.name: Rob Stanton
characters.description: Beth Ann's husband, an aerospace engineer at Cyther-Tech who enjoys the fruits of his wife's catering to him, and those given by the young blonde waitress in a diner. All Take and No Give: Rob's relationship with his wife in a nutshell. He never thinks past what would happen to Beth Ann if he were to die and only views her as someone who is subservient to him and can cook meals. He scoffs at Beth Ann's desire to do something that does not consists of taking care of his desires and dismisses the fact that she sacrificed her dreams of being a professional pianist to build a life with him.He also intends to repeat the pattern with April, upon finding out she is pregnant with his child Asshole Victim:No one will be sorry for his death, especially after it's revealed he's been deceiving Beth Ann into believing the death of their daughter washerfault and not a consequence to his cheating. Consummate Liar:Rob is this as later episodes reveal, with Beth Ann giving him one last chance to confess to his adultery being the reason that their daughter died. Even his mistress, April, lampshades this aspect of him with “men who cheat also know how to lie”. He still maintains his lies, to which Beth Ann responds that he's "made this all so much easier." Had he owned up to his actions, Beth Ann would have presumably given him a loaded gun to use against Ralph. Deliberate Values Dissonance: Rob is every bit as sexist as any man from the sixties, and Beth Ann doesn't think it unusual or have a problem with it (or at least, she claims she doesn't have a problem with it). Sheila recognizes and calls out how chauvinistic his behavior is, but her own husband deems it "militant" and reacts in amusement.

characters.name: April Warner
characters.description: Rob's mistress, a waitress at Jansen's Diner in Glendale who aspires to become a singer, she befriends "Sheila" (Beth Ann). Abusive Parents: April's father would physically abuse her mother, who then hid her black eyes under various makeup. Such a sight was so common that April still remembers the exact steps she'd take. The worst part is that everyone in her family knew, and looked the other way. Deliberate Values Dissonance: She’s not as bad as Rob, but she does at one point state a rather outdated belief that people who cheat on their spouses (particularly men) are in the right to do so once and if they grow bored of their wives, even for superficial reasons. Considering her role asThe Mistress, this isn’t that surprising. Good Girls Avoid Abortion:April decides to have an abortion when she's gotten pregnant by Rob, who's married, saying she can't care for a baby alone. Beth Ann isn't happy with this, but is mostly worried by her going to a back alley abortionist who might injure or kill her accidentally due to ignorance or the unsanitary conditions. She talks April out of it due to the danger. Moral Myopia:When she reads the fake letter Mary writes to Ralph saying she is leaving him for Rob, April calls Rob a bastard. Yet April dated a man she knew is married, and wasn’t conflicted about him leaving his wife for her. She also gets angry at Beth Ann for lying to her about her identity, ignoring the fact that she’s been willingly having an affair with the latter’s husband.

characters.name: Sheila Mosconi
characters.description: Beth Ann's mouthy, but loyal, neighbor who assists her in her schemes. Affectionate Nickname: Refers to Beth Ann as "honey". Brief Accent Imitation: She puts on a strained American accent as she pretends to be Beth Ann when April stops by the house claiming Rob left his jacket at the diner. However, she almost slips up a couple of times before catching herself. The Confidant: She serves as one for Beth Ann when the other vents about her unhappy marriage to Rob. Sheila is even the one to suggest Beth Ann confronts April about the affair. Deadpan Snarker: She and Leo are a mouthy Italian-American couple who have the gift of the gab and sharp wit to match. Sheila particularly has her owncompilationof her lines.

characters.name: Leo Mosconi
characters.description: Sheila's calmer husband, an owner of laundromats, who is very aware of Rob cheating on Beth Ann. Awful Wedded Life: Played for laughs. When at Beth Ann's housewarming party, Leo tries to get Sheila to dance with him, who turns him down for some pie and hands her daughter over to him. He then tells his daughter they'll discuss all of the other nice women "daddy should have married" as they both give each other sour side-eyes. However, out of some of the other characters, they do seem to be happy together. Deadpan Snarker: He and his wife a mouthy Italian-American couple who have the gift of the gab and sharp wit to match. Nouveau Riche: Sheila and her husband Leo are hinted as this: coming from Brooklyn and setting up a successful line of laundromats in Pasadena. Played straight with the loud and rather tacky behavior but subverted as they are often the most loyal and honest characters in the story.

characters.name: Mosconi Children
characters.description: Sheila and Leo's' badly behaved children.

characters.name: Emily Stanton
characters.description: Beth Ann and Rob's late daughter, who died in 1961 at age six. Posthumous Character: At the beginning of "I Was Just Wondering What Makes Dames Like You So Deadly", for each era we hear from a dead relative close to the protagonists; Beth Ann and Rob's daughter Emily talks about how she knows her motheris unhappy but Rob doesn't know because she smiles all the time, and she fears her mother will do something terrible.

characters.name: Mary Vlasin
characters.description: Beth Ann's neighbor, who is being abused by her husband. Domestic Abuse: Suffered this at the hands of Ralph. It's to the point when Beth Ann tries to help Mary during their housewarming party and suggests she stay the night, Mary sadly shakes her head and tells her, "it'll only make it worse". When Beth Ann goes to visit Mary at her home, Mary doesn't even try to hide her bruises, and claims her casted arm was due to falling on her own. Grass Is Greener: Despite Beth Ann trying to rationalize and indirectly end Rob's affair, Mary benevolently envies how strong she is as she is too scared of her physically abusive husband. "Not So Different" Remark: She observes how miserable Beth Ann is with her husband, but chooses to still stay with him. Mary calls both of their situations similar, and how the two of them aren't as different as Beth Ann seems to claim.Mary:We should be friends. Spiteful Spit: During the funerals montage, Mary can be seenstanding over the grave of her husband, lean over, and spit on it before calmly walking away.Mary:She ended up killing him... and I'm so glad she did.

characters.name: Ralph Vlasin
characters.description: Mary's abusive and controlling husband. Asshole Victim:No one will miss Mary's horrifically abusive husband Ralph, let alone Mary herself. Crazy Jealous Guy: Played terrifyingly straight. He gets angry at seeing Mary happily dance with Rob during Beth Ann's party, and violently drags her into another room to admonish her, claiming she was cheating on him. It's shown later with Mary's bruises and arm in a cast that he regularly abuses her.This is eventually weaponized, as Beth Ann baits him into murdering Rob by having Mary leave a false confession letter for him claiming that she's leaving him for Rob. Domestic Abuse: He regularly abuses Mary and gets violent at seeing her being happy. Killed Offscreen:Beth Ann informs Simone as she's selling the house that Ralph was executed 10 years after murdering her husband.

characters.name: Claire
characters.description: Rob's secretary and his former mistress. Foil: To Rob.Both were having sex the day Emily died, but while Rob kept on hiding the truth from Beth Ann and gaslit her into believing the death was her own fault, Claire eventually came to confess to Beth Ann about how she was the one who left the gate open. It's All My Fault:When Beth Ann and Emily came home early, Rob was having an afternoon tryst with Claire. In her haste to make a discreet escape through the backyard, she forgot to close the gate behind her, and Emily subsequently chased her new ball out into the street and got hit by a car. My God, What Have I Done?:Claire was the one who left the gate open, leading to Emily running out into the street and being hit. When she got the news an hour later at work, she immediately knew it was all because of her. Sexy Secretary: A pretty and fashionable secretarywho used to sleep with her boss.

characters.name: Simone Grove
characters.description: A dramatic and fashionable socialite who’s been divorced twice before marrying Karl. She later learns of his infidelity and true sexuality when she receives an anonymous envelope containing photos of him kissing another man and starts an affair with her neighbor’s son to get back at him. Aw, Look! They Really Do Love Each Other: Simone and Karl. Even with her finding out he's gay then having an affair, they bond whenKarl has AIDS and Simone sticks by him through it all, including selling her belongings to pay his medical bills. In the end, Simone fulfills his wish to kill him and end it before he suffers too much with each confessing the other is "the love of my life." The Beard: Simone learns she was unknowingly serving as one to Karl, who's a closeted gay man. Character Development: Simone starts the show as aRich Bitchbutdecades later, she's become happy with a simpler life and dedicating herself to charity work after Karl's death. Everyone Has Standards: Simone might be starting an affair with someone who's barely legal, but she draws the line at anythingactuallyillegal and promptly sends Tommy home when he says he'll be 18 "in two days".Refuses to go to Amy's wedding when she declares that she doesn't want Karl, who has been Amy's primary father figure, to walk her down the aisle due to the social opprobrium she will face over his HIV/AIDS diagnosis.

characters.name: Karl Grove
characters.description: Simone’s third husband, whose secret homosexuality is revealed by photos of him kissing another man being sent to his wife. He later contracts AIDS. Aw, Look! They Really Do Love Each Other: Even with Simone finding out he's gay then having an affair, they bond whenKarl has AIDS and Simone sticks by him through it all, including selling her belongings to pay his medical bills. In the end, Simone fulfills his wish to kill him and end it before he suffers too much with each confessing the other is "the love of my life." Deadpan Snarker: He is particularly snarky around Simone and even his beloved stepdaughter Amy. Has his owncompilation. Forced Out of the Closet: Karl has no choice but to confess his homosexuality to his wife after she finds pictures of him kissing another man. Good Stepmother: Gender inverted with Karl, who has been a loving and constant father figure to Simone's daughter Amy.

characters.name: Tommy Harte
characters.description: Simone’s neighbor, her best friend’s eighteen-year-old son, whom she starts an affair with. Character Development: Starts off hostile towards Karl due to the hurt and embarrassment he caused Simone, and sees him as an obstacle. Over time, he warms up to Simone's husband and shows compassion towards him after his HIV/AIDS diagnosis. Diving Save: Tommy dives on Simone when Naomi tries to kill her, pushing her out of the way of the car. Hidden Depths: Is a very talented artist, even as a teenager. Likes Older Women: Turns 18 between episodes 1 and 2 and begins an affair with Simone, who is in her late 40s to early 50s.

characters.name: Naomi Harte
characters.description: Simone’s next-door neighbor and best friend, and Tommy’s mother. Disowned Parent: Tommy disowns her for trying to ruin Karl and Simone's lives. False Rape Accusation: Tells the receptionist at the hospital where Tommy stays after his car accident that Simone has been molesting Tommy since he was a child. Jerkass Has a Point: Her eighteen-year-old son spends $10,000 on a piece of jewelry, crashes his car while driving drunk, and gets Simone's face tattooed on his body. That’s not even to mention he had JUST turned eighteen and Simone initially started the affair just to get back at Naomi. She has plenty of valid reasons to disapprove and be concerned about his relationship with Simone,she just goes overboard in her response, with that being the reason Tommy disowns her. May–December Romance: Naomi (who is hinted to be aGold Digger) and her deceased husband Edmund (who died at 57 prior to the series); there is a family photo of a grade-school aged Tommy with the youthful and blonde Naomi with a graying and older man. Zigzagged when the elder Harte revealed in a post mortem voiceover that his marriage with Naomi wasn't a happy one.

characters.name: Amy Lin
characters.description: Simone’s daughter from her first marriage. Bratty Teenage Daughter: Amy is likely in her late teens or early twenties since she says she's hardly older than Tommy (who's eighteen). Shadow Archetype: What distinguishes Amy from her mother Simone. She has a chance to show Karl how much she loves him when she finds out that he hasAIDS, but instead she tells him not to come to her wedding so that more people won't cancel. Simone is horrified by Amy's selfishness, especially since it causes her to realize she’s part of the reason why Amy turned out to be this way and was just like her before herCharacter Development. Spoiled Brat: Like her mother Simone, Amy is spoiled, immature, demanding, and very loud. Unlike Simone, Amy doesn’t get better.

characters.name: Hector
characters.description: Simone’s former hairdresser, who stopped taking her out of guilt when he started seeing Karl behind her back.

characters.name: Taylor Harding
characters.description: Action Girl: Downplayed. She is a very independent modern woman who is not afraid to assert herself,although she does get a bit of an action scene when Jade attacks her, and she has to kill her in self-defense. Be Careful What You Wish For: She wants an exciting woman in her life,and gets the psychotic Jade. Hidden Depths:Taylor, despite seeming like a fiercely independent working woman, in actuality resents having to shoulder all the responsibility as the breadwinner for her and Eli, and part of the reason why she fell for Jade is because she alleviates some of Taylor’s stress. Ms. Fanservice: Wears a black one-piece swimsuit in a hot tub in episode 2. Unwitting Instigator of Doom: Bringing Jade into her marriage nearly getsher AND Eli killed, and causes him to relapse.

characters.name: Eli Cohen
characters.description: Amazon Chaser: In the story of how him and Taylor met, he claims he was immediately turned on by her giving an impassioned speech at a woman’s march. He’s also a content househusband in the present,though it gets downplayed when it’s revealed he’s more insecure and emasculated than he appears to be. Immediate Self-Contradiction:Eli pretends to still love Jade and reassures her that she's not a bad person, then rushes out and snaps at Taylor for leaving him alone with a psychopath. Manchild: Eli has shades of this, as he sometimes acts more like a lazy teenager still living at home than an adult man. For one, he tends to be irresponsible with his spending, and seems much more interested in playing with his amenities instead of doing any actual writing or completing chores around his house, with Taylor having to remind him of his responsibilities.This actually stresses Taylor out due to the increased workload she must now take on for the both of them. It doesn’t help that Jade proves to be a bad influence on him which causes him to relapse to his old drugs problems.Eventually, after he finally talks things out with Taylor and the experience with Jade has ended badly, he gets a little better. Most Writers Are Writers: Eli is a scriptwriter. Off the Wagon: Eli falls off the wagon after Jade gives him a pill to help his writing process.

characters.name: Jade
characters.description: Cool Car: Owns a red Infiniti Q60.Too bad she wasn't paying attention on the road as she crashes into a Volvo. The Dulcinea Effect: Eli is immediately infatuated with Jade when he sees her strip off at the pool and becomes just as dependent on her as Taylor. Manic Pixie Dream Girl: Deconstructed. Jade is a beautiful, young, spirited woman who immediately relieves burdens on both Eli and Taylor.And she's insane. Ms. Fanservice: Gets two scenes in her underwear and a bikini. Only One Name: Taylor and Eli only know her as Jade.Her real name is Irene Dubrovnik, and it's implied that the one name is used to help her stay hidden.

characters.name: Alma Fillcot
characters.description: Alma is a timid and awkward housewife, who remains optimistic in the face of the world’s cruelty. Alma yearns for a spot in the local garden club and to see her ungainly daughter married, but her life is disrupted once she learns of her husband’s secret hobby. '20s Bob Haircut: Alma starts off with a similar hairstyle to this, albeit more prim and plain, as befitting her image of "a frump" who hasn't updated her wardbrobe in the last 15 years much less 5. Arc Villain: Becomes this during the second half followingmanipulating Bertram to kill Carlo in Episode Six. Beauty Is Bad:As Alma becomes more aggressive and manipulative, she goes from "frump" to a beautiful, vain woman. Beneath Suspicion: Invoked. Rita says that she never even looked twice at Alma, which Alma says was why she turned to the dark side.

characters.name: Rita Castillo
characters.description: Rita is the sardonic wife to the cruel but wealthy Carlo Castillo. As she waits for her elderly husband to die, Rita runs the Elysian Park Garden Club with an iron fist and spends much of her time engaging in an affair with a much younger man. Arc Villain: Is the main threat of the first half of the season before being replaced byAlmaduring the second half. Aloof Dark-Haired Girl: Rita has black hair and she's a pretty aloof, snobby person. Berserk Button: Rita doesn't like to be reminded of her former profession as a prostitute. Blackmail: Rita has Scooter seduce Catherine so Vern can take photos of them while they're having sex to use so Catherine's disinherited and will leave.

characters.name: Scooter Polarsky
characters.description: Brainless Beauty: Scooter isn't a complete idiot, but is rather dim-witted and gets along mainly due to being quite handsome (including attracting smarter women). Beauty Is Bad: Scooter is a dumb person, but he invokes this when he tells Dee that he hopes their baby won't be handsome, because it's better to be ordinary-looking and "not expect so much out of life." Jerk with a Heart of Gold: While he is a cheater and a liar, Scooter still cares about Rita enough to give her money when she loses everything after being freed from prison. He also leaves the hospital immediately afterbeing shotwhen he learns about Deeand their baby, offering to be there for both of them. Mr. Fanservice: Scooter is quite the handsome man, and he plays up his good looks to seduce Catherine, such as by stripping to the waist in front of her. Saying Too Much: Because ScooterThought They Knew Already, he tells Dee that Alma told him about Dee's baby.

characters.name: Catherine Castillo
characters.description: Alliterative Name:CatherineCastillo. Karma Houdini:Catherine, who gets away with shooting Scooter and Bertram, and trying to ruin Rita's life, before going back to Texas with her chauffeur and her inheritance. She isn't even seen in the finale. Letting Her Hair Down: Catherine after Scooter starts to woo her starts to wear her hair long and hanging. Prim and Proper Bun: Before her turn towards the sexual and significantly nicer, she wears her hair back in a tight bun. When She Smiles: The dour Catherine, according to Scooter, has a very nice smile.

characters.name: Vern Loomis
characters.description: Nice Guy: Vern treats Dee with genuine kindness and appreciates her strength of character. The Smart Guy: Vern was able to put together the clues thatBertram and especially Alma were involved in Carlo and Isabel's murders. He has reasons to believe Alma was more likely to kill Carlo and Isabel based on his meeting with her. Twofer Token Minority: While this season is significantly more diverse, Vern is still the single black member of the cast, and the only disabled one.

characters.name: Isabel Vega
characters.description: Blackmail: Isabel tries to blackmail Alma and Bertram with one of the photos of Scooter and Catherine, which show Alma's presence the night Carlo was murdered. The Heavy: WhileIsabel didn't actually kill Rita's first husband, she's also the person who tried to shoot him. No Hero to His Valet: Isabel, Rita's maid, having no issue with speaking her mind and pointing out how foolish or even dangerous Rita's scheming ishas become subverted in that Isabel is Rita's cousin all along.
